name: Chat
description: A conversation: incoming bubbles at the start edge, the reader's own inverted at the end, a typing indicator and quick-reply buttons.
whenToUse: A scripted "say hi" section on a marketing page that hands off to email or LinkedIn.
whenNotToUse: Comments and threads on a document — use a list of cards.

classes.ayy-chat: Root. role="log" when messages arrive live, so they're announced.
classes.ayy-chat__message: One message row: an optional avatar and its bubble.
classes.ayy-chat__message--out: Sent by the reader: end edge, primary colours.
classes.ayy-chat__bubble: The bubble. The corner by the avatar is squared off.
classes.ayy-chat__typing: Three pulsing dots inside a bubble while a reply is written. Give it role="img" and an aria-label.
classes.ayy-chat__replies: Quick replies under the conversation: small outline buttons, at the end edge.

js: chatMessageClass({ direction?, className? }) → string; chatClass, chatBubbleClass, chatTypingClass, chatRepliesClass constants.

react.import: import { Chat, ChatMessage, ChatTyping, ChatReplies } from "ayywi/react";

ChatMessage.renders: <div class="ayy-chat__message"> with the avatar and a bubble around children

props.avatar: ReactNode — e.g. an Avatar size sm.

ChatTyping.renders: A message whose bubble holds the typing dots

a11y: Use role="log" on the conversation when messages arrive while the reader watches; they're announced politely, in order.
The typing dots are an image with a name ("Dani is typing"); remove the element when the message lands.
Quick replies are real buttons; after one is chosen, move focus to the next sensible place, not back to the top.
do: Keep bubbles short; split long answers into several messages.
Pair incoming messages with the sender's avatar the first time.
dont: Don't auto-scroll the page while someone is reading above.
Don't use colour alone to tell who's speaking; the side and avatar do it too.
